terra.problem: Says Zechariah does not panic or sprint off. The text does not say how he reacts beyond asking his question.
Says Zechariah stays put. The text does not describe his movements.
Says Zechariah stays right where he is. The text does not say that.
Describes the patrol as walking a route. The passage describes horses and riders, not a walking patrol.
Says the riders come back with their report. The text records their report but does not say they return.
Says the next verse answers how long mercy will be withheld. It records kind and comforting words, but does not give a length of time.
Says the riders have come back. The passage says they report their patrol, not that they return.
Claims to know why the baker would pick this answer, though Papa Dorin has not been told.
Saying the nations did the opposite of rebuilding goes beyond the text. It says they added to the calamity, not that they destroyed what was rebuilt.
The final sentence is vague and generic rather than explaining the promise in Papa Dorin's voice.
The explanation repeats the answer and comments that it is short, without adding a meaningful explanation or much of Papa Dorin's voice.
Says the horns get scared. The text says the craftsmen have come to terrify them, not that this has already happened.
Says the horns are now thrown down. The text says the craftsmen have come to throw them down.
Says the horns get terrified and thrown down. The passage states what the craftsmen have come to do, not the outcome.
Says the horns go down as an accomplished outcome. The text says the craftsmen have come to throw them down.
Says Judah was scattered so far that no one could lift his head. The text gives no distance or extent as the reason.
Papa Dorin comments on his own storytelling by saying he will not joke about the passage.
